abstract: B cells and their clonally rearranged B-cell receptors (BCRs) form the cellular and molecular basis of humoral immunity. Single-cell RNA sequencing coupled with V(D)J profiling now enables BCR clonotypes to be linked directly to B-cell transcriptional states; however, existing immune-receptor resources are often T-cell/TCR-oriented or limited in BCR-specific analytical depth. Here, we present X-BCRdb, a cross-disease single-cell database for integrated analysis of BCR repertoires, B-cell transcriptional states, and clonal evolution. The current release harmonizes 61 studies, 1401 samples, and 903 subjects across 45 disease or physiological categories and 13 tissue groups. It contains 2 402 995 processed B-lineage cells, including 1 565 870 cells with matched transcriptome and BCR information, and 3 993 244 annotated BCR records. A unified analytical workflow supports standardized B-cell annotation and BCR repertoire characterization, including clonotype assignment, SHM profiling, isotype analysis, VH/VL pairing, lineage reconstruction, and public clonotype analysis. The web interface links these receptor features with B-cell transcriptional states across individual samples, studies and diseases, and provides global CDR3 similarity search, data download, and API access. X-BCRdb is freely available at https://xbcrdb.net/ and provides a systematic platform for studying disease-associated B-lineage-cell responses and facilitating the prioritization of candidate BCR sequences for downstream antibody discovery and functional validation.
